f2.windows_job:
This is the new job `window` ("desktop window check (windows-latest)") in .github/workflows/desktop.yml. It runs after `build`, on every run of the Desktop app workflow. The workflow's path filters now also include testenv/src/bench/**, testenv/src/provider/** and scripts/desktop-window-check.*. The job has a 40-minute timeout and should take about 6 to 10 minutes after the build.

How it runs, step by step:
1. Checks out the repo and sets up Node 22. It needs no pnpm install, because the driver uses only Node built-ins and apps/mobile/e2e/cdp.mjs and webview-console.mjs.
2. Downloads the build job's artifact `desktop-windows-latest`.
3. Installs the MSI into Program Files with msiexec /qn, logging to RUNNER_TEMP. It fails on a non-zero exit and prints the end of the log. It then puts the installed exe's path in FR_APP_EXE.
4. Runs `node scripts/desktop-window-check.mjs --exe $FR_APP_EXE --home "$RUNNER_TEMP\fr window\Zürich home" --out $RUNNER_TEMP\window-check`. The ü is built with [char]0x00FC, so the YAML stays ASCII.
5. Uploads the out folder as the artifact `desktop-window-check`, also when the step fails.

What the script does:
(a) installStandIn copies testenv/package.json, testenv/src/bench and testenv/src/provider into <install>\runtime\testenv. That is where `fr daemon --provider bench` looks (BENCH_ENTRY in packages/runtime/src/cli/main.ts). Without these files the installed app refuses the stand-in. I checked this against a locally built payload: its daemon started with --provider bench and planned a brief.
(b) It starts a link page on 127.0.0.1 that records every request.
(c) It spawns the installed exe with no arguments. windowEnv sets: FORERUNNER_HOME (fresh); FORERUNNER_DAEMON_PROVIDER=bench (new shell switch); WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS=--remote-debugging-port=9333; FORERUNNER_VAULT_BACKEND=file; FORERUNNER_SANDBOX_ENGINE=podman (so Settings shows "Get Docker Desktop"); FORERUNNER_BENCH_DELAY_MS=100. It removes model credentials, GH/GitHub tokens and every other FORERUNNER_* variable.
(d) Waits for <home>\runtime\daemon.json and /health.
   - Assert: the daemon starts.
   - Assert: daemon-shell.log contains `[shell] the daemon runs on the stand-in model "bench"`.
(e) Waits for a page target on the DevTools endpoint whose URL is on an app origin (tauri://localhost or http(s)://tauri.localhost, not the splash), connects with cdp.mjs connectPage, and forwards the page console as `webview:` lines.
(f) Walks the journey and screenshots every step with Page.captureScreenshot, saving each step's text too.
   - Set up later, when the assistant is shown. Assert: it goes away.
   - Home, then New project with a name and the one-line brief "A page that shows a random quote", then Create project. Assert, required: the URL becomes /projects/<id>.
   - Polls GET /projects/:id/intake. Assert, required: state is pending.
   - Inbox link, then the card data-testid=request with `Plan for "<name>"`. Assert, required: exactly 1 card with at least 1 intake-task line.
   - Approve and start. Assert: the text "Plan approved: N tasks written" appears.
   - Assert, required: a session for the project exists within 60 s, from GET /sessions.
   - Home, then the project card, and waits for the session's end. Assert: status completed.
   - Assert: every task from GET /projects/:id/tasks is done.
   - Overview tab, then Tasks tab. Assert: every done title is in the page text.
(g) Shell hand-offs. Each one is read from <home>\logs\desktop-shell.log after the log's byte offset, parsed by parseHandoffs.
   - PR link. seedPrUrl writes task.pr_url into <home>\data\state.sqlite (node:sqlite) as http://127.0.0.1:<port>/acme/window-check/pull/1. Then Overview, then Tasks to refetch. Required: exactly one data-testid=pr-link. Clicking it must produce `handed to the system browser (link): <that URL>`. The window URL must be unchanged and on the app origin. Whether the link page received a GET is a non-required note.
   - A target=_blank anchor injected via Runtime.evaluate and clicked with CDP mouse events. Must produce a hand-off with via "new window" to the link page URL. The window must stay put.
   - An injected file:///C:/Windows/win.ini link. Nothing but a refusal may be logged, and the window must stay put.
   - Overview, then data-testid=folder-open. Must produce `handed to the file manager: <folder>`. That folder must equal the Overview's folder-path text (sameFolder ignores case and slash direction on Windows). folder-note must not say "did not open", and the window must stay put.
   - Settings link (aria-label Settings), then data-testid=sandbox-docker-link. Must produce a hand-off of https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/ and the window must stay put. If the link is missing, the check is required only when GET /sandbox says not_installed.
   - Note only: no uncaught page exception.
   - When a hand-off line is missing, the failure detail quotes the shell's own lines about browser, refused or could not.
(h) Teardown:
   - POST /shutdown, then wait for /health to stop answering.
   - `taskkill /PID <app pid> /T /F`, only the PID the script started.
   - Copy desktop-shell.log, daemon-shell.log and model-calls.jsonl.
   - Write result.json, append the step summary, and exit 1 if any required check failed.

The shell changes this relies on (commit ea132f5):
- windows.rs logs info `handed to the system browser (link|new window): <origin+path>`, never the query, fragment or credentials, and logs refusals with how the link came.
- folder.rs logs `handed to the file manager: <folder>`.
- supervisor.rs `daemon_flags` turns FORERUNNER_DAEMON_PROVIDER into `daemon --provider <name>`, only for fake, bench and bench-live. Unset or empty adds nothing. Any other value is refused with a warning and never forwarded.
- spawn_daemon now takes the environment (`&impl Env`). Its callers in actions.rs and selftest.rs pass ProcessEnv.

The hand-off lines themselves, which only the shell writes. Need 'ok' on: clicking PR hands the pull request to the system browser (via link); a target="_blank" link via new window; a file: link handed to no program; Open folder with the same folder as shown; Get Docker Desktop; and every 'the window stays on the app's page after ...'. The Linux sandbox job on a hosted runner: buildx loading forerunner-runner:local from the real Dockerfile (COPY . . invalidates the pnpm install layer on every commit, about 1 to 3 minutes); the daemon as uid 1001 with rootful Docker (--user 1001:gid, so files are owned by the runner); docker events on the hosted engine. Look at the step summary 'Full-review task in the Docker sandbox (Linux)'. Expect 20 ok lines, in particular 'the file belongs to this user, not to root' with uid 1001 (here it ran as root, uid 0) and 'the task's command ran inside the container'.

The real runner image (built from the Dockerfile with build-essential and the full repo) was not used here. A stand-in node:22-bookworm-slim image was tagged forerunner-runner:local, so the full image's runtime behaviour in the sandbox shows only in CI.
risks: The PR link's pr_url is written straight into the daemon's SQLite store (seedPrUrl), not set by the PR flow, because no daemon route sets it. This proves the Tasks tab link and the shell's hand-off, not the PR executor. A follow-up could use testenv/src/githost with a linked repository instead.

FORERUNNER_SANDBOX_ENGINE=podman is set only so that Settings shows the 'Get Docker Desktop' link. If podman is installed on the Windows runner, the state is not not_installed, the link does not show, and the check is reported as not required. It does not fail.

FORERUNNER_DAEMON_PROVIDER is a new switch in a shipped binary. It only forwards fake, bench or bench-live, and bench and bench-live refuse without testenv/. `fake`, though, would start an installed app on the echo provider if a person set the variable. It is documented as development and CI only in apps.md.
The window job needs the whole build matrix (`needs: build`), so a Linux build failure skips it.
The cdp.mjs driver was written for the Android WebView. Its click guard and the fallback ladder are untested on WebView2.
If WebView2 ignores the environment variable, the whole window check fails at attach. Nothing else in the workflow is affected.
The sandbox job builds the image a second time, in parallel with the sandbox-image job, reading the gha cache only. On a cold cache it can take several minutes.
I could not run actionlint (its download was refused). The workflows were only YAML-parsed and structure-checked.
The scratchpad is shared with another agent: msg2.txt was overwritten after my commit. The commits themselves are not affected.

blocking.issue: FIXED in f6f9bb0. The Docker sandbox check had a step that could never fail: "the file belongs to this user, not to root" (scripts/sandbox-full-review.mjs). testing.md presented it as proof that the container runs as the host uid on rootful Docker.
blocking.evidence: ContainerSandbox.writeFile (packages/runtime/src/sandbox/container.ts:587) calls writeWorktreeFile on the host. So the daemon writes src/greet.js as the daemon's own user, whatever user the container ran as. The script compares that to its own uid, which is the same user. Inside the container the stand-in coder only runs `node --check src/greet.js` (testenv/src/bench/role-player.ts:596), and that writes nothing. The builder's run had uid 0 vs 0, and mine was the same.
blocking.expected: No check that cannot fail, and docs that say what is really proven. I removed the check, rewrote the header comment and testing.md step 6, and added the container's user to "Not covered". The --user default is pinned by packages/runtime/test/sandbox-factory.test.ts:66 and the adapter's integration test.

blocking.issue: FIXED in f6f9bb0. The window check did not always save a screenshot of the failure. A journey that stopped (a must() or a CDP click/timeout error) left no picture of the state where it stopped, only the step before. A stop before the window's page answered on DevTools (no daemon, no page target) left no screenshot at all. That is exactly the case the first, never-run Windows job is most likely to hit.
blocking.evidence: In the original main(), `shot` existed only after connectPage. The catch block only recorded a check, and the finally block copied logs but took no screenshot. The task's criterion: "always saves screenshots and logs as artifacts".
blocking.expected: A screenshot where the journey stopped. Now `shot` is hoisted and the catch block captures the page at the stop. With --exe it also captures the whole screen through a new exported desktopScreenshot (Windows PowerShell CopyFromScreen, path passed only through the FR_SHOT env var), so a shell dialog or a window that never appeared is in the artifact. Unit tests added. I verified it with an --attach run that had a planted stop: 06-stopped-the-inbox-shows-the-plan-card-...png was saved.

non_blocking: Committed with --ignore-other-worktrees: fix/f2-ci-checks was also checked out in the builder's worktree .claude/worktrees/wf_a9db00a9-443-2, so the branch is now at f6f9bb0 there while that worktree's files are still at 3ae158c. Git there will show my changes reversed as uncommitted edits. Do not commit or stash from that worktree; merge the branch ref f6f9bb0. Nothing was pushed.

Hardening in the same commit: WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS now also carries wry's own --disable-features list (msWebOOUI, msPdfOOUI, msSmartScreenProtection; WebView2 may use the variable instead of the app's arguments) plus CalculateNativeWinOcclusion. Reason: once the PR click opens the system browser over the window, occlusion tracking may stop painting the page, and cdp.mjs clicks wait for requestAnimationFrame. This is speculative but harmless.

The window job has never run on a Windows runner (no push was allowed), so its first CI run is the real test. Some evidence it can work: Desktop app run 41339376222 (windows-latest) shows installed-check.ps1 starting the installed exe in the runner session itself ("running before the uninstall (the app): forerunner-desktop, node, node"), and the MSI is the only file in the desktop-windows-latest artifact. Still unproven: that WebView2 opens --remote-debugging-port in this release build, and how the runner's first-run system browser behaves.

The file: link check probably never reaches the shell: WebView2/Chromium blocks a file: navigation from an http origin before NavigationStarting fires. So it checks the outcome (nothing is opened, the window stays put), not windows.rs's refusal path. It can still fail if anything is handed off. Its detail now says when no refusal was logged either.
The PR-link check accepts either via (link or new window). In the shell, ExternalLink has no target, so it should always be "link". It could be tightened to require via === "link".
"Open folder shows no error" reads folder-note right after the hand-off line appears. That is weak but can fail (the UI showing an error although the shell succeeded).
The window job's `needs: build` waits for both matrix legs, so a failing Linux build skips the Windows window check.

sandbox-full-review.mjs: if startDaemon fails, bench lib's fail() calls process.exit(1), so there is no result.json and no step summary. The daemon log is still in the uploaded <out>/bench/daemon.log and its tail is printed.

The shell change is safe. FORERUNNER_DAEMON_PROVIDER is read only from the process environment (ProcessEnv), which a web page cannot set. It is limited to an allowlist (fake, bench, bench-live) and forwarded as an argv entry, never through a shell. bench and bench-live still need testenv/ copied into the install. windows.rs and folder.rs only add logging: the navigation and new-window decisions are unchanged, and the log drops query, fragment and credentials (loggable_url). The self-test forwards the variable too (documented).

No secrets in logs or artifacts. windowEnv and bench daemonEnv strip model credentials, GH/GitHub tokens and every FORERUNNER_* variable. result.json files carry the daemon URL and pid, never the token. The token is a redacted Secret in the shell log.

Flake seen once in pnpm check under load 11+ on 4 CPUs: packages/runtime/test/monthly-jobs-wiring.test.ts (calibration notification not raised within settle()). It is unrelated to this branch: it passed alone and in the other two full runs.
review.what_i_checked:
Reviewed fix/f2-ci-checks (3ae158c: ea132f5, 933e3d4, 3ae158c), then added review fix f6f9bb0 (signed, with the trailers, not pushed).

Workflow YAML. actionlint was blocked here, so instead I parsed both files with PyYAML and read them closely:
- Job `window` (desktop.yml) runs on windows-latest after build; `desktop-windows-latest` is the build job's artifact name; GITHUB_ENV is written as UTF-8 without BOM in pwsh; the ü comes from [char]0x00FC; path filters were widened.
- Job `sandbox-full-review` (ci.yml) runs on ubuntu-latest; env.PNPM_VERSION is defined; build-push-action loads the image and only reads the GHA cache; .dockerignore keeps node_modules out of the context; the upload runs if: always().

Assertions. Every check in both scripts was read for whether it can fail. Two problems turned up, both listed under blocking above.

Docker job, run for real. I ran it twice against a private dockerd 29.9.2 (vfs, no bridge, mirror.gcr.io node:22-bookworm-slim tagged forerunner-runner:local), stopped by its own PID afterwards:
- Before the fix: 20/20.
- After the fix: 19/19.
- docker events show the container created from the image with the task's label, `timeout -s KILL 60 node --check src/greet.js` run by docker exec with exit 0, and the container destroyed.
- The model-call log shows critic calls labelled "critic tier 2 on task <id>" (from packages/critic/src/critic.ts:478).
- A tier-2 task without a container engine is refused (factory.ts, U-079), so this is not the process sandbox.

Window check:
- Read in full against apps/mobile/e2e/cdp.mjs (timeouts come back as "X: not within N s" or as CdpError messages), windows.rs, folder.rs, FolderPath.tsx, ExternalLink.tsx and SandboxSettingsCard.tsx. The Docker link appears when the state is not_installed on a non-Linux platform, which the podman override produces.
- The log goes to <home>/logs/desktop-shell.log at Info level (lib.rs), and app_dirs honours FORERUNNER_HOME.
- --attach dry runs on a bench (daemon + vite) in headless Chrome: every required check passed, and with a planted stop the stop screenshot was saved.

Shell (Rust): cargo fmt --check, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, and cargo test (135 passed, including the 4 new tests), with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/frbench/cargo-target.

Docs: apps.md, testing.md and validation.md were updated; docs-check --base f64d7e9 passes.

pnpm check:
- Green on the reviewed head (4287 passed).
- One run on the fix hit the load flake noted under non-blocking.
- Green on the committed fix f6f9bb0: 421 files, 4289 tests, lint, paths, typecheck, link-check and secret-scan.
